title: Charles IX to Philibert du Croc, undated (1565–1567 or 1572), DECODE R2789

steps.what: Opened DECODE R2789 with the user's authenticated session and exported both manuscript pages.
Read Destray's cited edition and found the same facsimile on Gallica; it identifies the item as document XLIII, without place or date.
Followed the cited Cryptiana prior art and found George Lasry's complete-page plaintext overlays published in 2022.
Compared the DECODE scans, Destray's Gallica facsimile, and Lasry's overlays; page layout, signatures, and every visible line correspond.
Transcribed the published overlay diplomatically and normalized its secure substance, retaining all visible gaps and uncertain phrases.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): READING.md (the project's transcription of Lasry's overlay) and cryptiana GL.htm as decryptions; no ciphertext transcription (project work).
Read bar applied per document (v10): 1 of 1 documents marked read measure under 95% of words read as sense (v2_score explicit holes) and are now read in part; read_share recorded for each.

outcome.method_basis: George Lasry's plaintext overlays of both pages were on Tomokiyo's cryptiana GL.htm (25 May 2022) before the attempt; the work compared them with the DECODE R2789 scans and Destray's 1924 facsimile and transcribed the overlay.
outcome.notes: The prior solution reads the letter in substance but leaves several signs or short phrases unresolved. No new cryptanalytic solve is claimed.

texts.label: Charles IX to Philibert du Croc, undated (1565-67 or 1572)
texts.summary: Charles IX tells his ambassador in Scotland, Philibert du Croc, to use his judgment and follow his instructions for the country's peace; above all his nephew, the young James VI, is to be well brought up, keep the Scots' traditional attachment to France, and not marry before Charles has been told and can send his intention. The postscript orders him to keep the English from gaining a foothold in Scotland. READING.md is a working transcription of George Lasry's plaintext overlay published on Tomokiyo's cryptiana GL.htm (25 May 2022), with its gaps kept.
texts.note: No transcription of the cipher signs exists (project work); the letter is printed in facsimile in Destray, Philibert Du Croc (1924), doc. XLIII. 24 Oct 2026: 92.8% of the words of R2789_reading.md read as sense (v2_score explicit holes); coherent sentences but under the 95% read bar, so read in part.
